claims.text: refund-requirements.md@stage-2 lines 3-4: a draft by the product owner and the Đơn Hàng team for stakeholders to comment on before Sprint 15 planning; the design is in docs/design/refund-design.md.

Lines 6-12: the problem starts from the meeting notes' decision that paid orders cannot be cancelled from the app and the customer must ask for a refund; today that means calling customer care, a manual refund on the gateway's admin page, and an email to accounting.
At stage-2, PATCH /api/v1/orders/{id}/cancel still cancels a paid order (Order.Cancel() only blocks cancelled and shipped); only the app has no way to cancel it.

Lines 14-25: two goals (customers request refunds without calling; accounting reconciles each refund without asking); four out-of-scope items: partial refunds, shipped orders (an open question from the notes, operations answers), cash-on-delivery orders, staff creating requests for customers.

Lines 27-39: six functional requirements YC-1..YC-6 (own paid order only; others refused with no change; full amount; no second request; confirmed refund cancels the order and emails; refused refund listed for staff with the gateway's reason); none names a class, table or endpoint.

Lines 41-50: a second list YC-7..YC-10 about how well the system must work; lines 52-59: an open-questions table with columns question, who answers, deadline (e.g. gateway refund window: gateway provider, PO asks, first week of Sprint 15; bank transfer; list format: accounting).
YC-4 says that after sending a request the customer sees the order being refunded and cannot send a second request for the same order.

A requirements document holds what a feature's stories share; requirements should be numbered, checkable, about what not how, and name no table or endpoint, because that is a design decision; unanswered questions go in with an owner instead of being guessed.
